# What this program tests {.unnumbered}

**Thesis.** The audit of the ISLA (Invariant Slice Attention) research record
([companion review](../cross_dataset_generalization/index.qmd)) concluded that
the record does not establish a cross-dataset accuracy advantage, and that the
promising targets are a complete physical input, a stable computational
representation, and reusable components of the physical response. This program
turns that agenda into experiments with preregistered bars, in the order the
audit recommended: first the controls that make any later result
interpretable (paired physical conditions, source-only normalization, and a
pressure-offset versus spatial-error decomposition), then, in parallel, the
computational-support study on the existing DrivAerML volume task and the
nonlearned gates for the three response-based directions (boundary-response
rank and basis transfer, local-response composition, solver correction
spaces). A separate chapter asks what classical solvers do that learned
surrogates do not, as a source of further hypotheses.

**Utility.** The quantity that matters is field and force error on
geometries and dataset families outside the training distribution, with the
PDE, boundary conditions, dimensionless parameters and label convention
stated; with query and mesh consistency; and with the total cost counted
(preprocessing, target-operator access, iterations, adaptation labels). A
result that improves a fixed-mesh in-family score without moving that
quantity is not progress here.

**How to read this.** Every chapter states current knowledge and the
preregistered bar that would change it; the dated record of what was tried,
in what order, is the notebook. Numbers in chapters are computed from
checked-in artifacts under `studies/`. Verdicts follow bars written before
the readout; amendments to an instrument are recorded before its numbers are
read. Architectures are named (ISLA, GeoTransolver, Transolver); ratios are
baseline error divided by ISLA error unless a chapter says otherwise.

| C1 | RUNNING | Is the zero-shot fastback error (ISLA 0.99, GeoTransolver 0.59, relative L2) a pressure-reference offset or a spatial error? An offset cancels from closed-surface forces and points at label conventions, not architecture. | AUDIT; saved predictions exist | Preregistered in @sec-nb-c1-prereg: offset-dominated if the constant carries ≥ 50% of area-weighted squared error for the source-only arms; spatial if ≤ 20% | pending |

Exact potential-flow labels. | C1 (if the offset does not explain the gap) | A model without the condition flag is bounded below by the equal-mixture floor; with the flag it reaches the in-distribution error | pending |
| D1 | PLANNED | Does a problem-derived computational support with passive readout keep the interacting configuration's interior accuracy while making output batching immaterial? | C1, C2; node budget from the main program | Pressure, velocity, eddy viscosity within 3% of the interacting arm at matched depth and inputs; zero structural query dependence; bf16 drift within a measured floor | pending |
| D2 | RUNNING | Does the boundary response, minus its principal part and null modes, compress and transfer across topology and gaps? | AUDIT | Residual reaches 1% at ≤ 1/3 of the full rank on held-out families; source-fitted basis within 2x of the oracle | pending |
| D3 | RUNNING | Do local port responses compose stably into new assemblies at useful cost? | AUDIT | Global energy error ≤ 5% at 1e-2 local error from 2 to 8 components; transfer-optimal rank ≤ 1/4 of the port dimension for 1% | pending |
| D4 | RUNNING | Does a frozen source-fitted correction space beat an equal-dimension classical coarse space on held-out systems, at common accuracy and total cost? | AUDIT | ≥ 2x contraction per unit work on slow modes within family, ≥ 1.5x under topology shift; ≥ 20% fewer total matvecs with setup amortized | pending |
| L | RUNNING | What do classical solvers do that learned surrogates do not, and which of those mechanisms can be learned or transferred? | AUDIT | A ranked list of mechanisms each with a falsifiable experiment | pending |
